# 隐藏组名的语义复核规则

This is a pre-specified evaluation of research candidates. You are not the generator. Use only the supplied records. Do not use tools, files, memory, network or external papers. Record what the evidence permits. Return JSON directly, with no markdown. No private reasoning trace is requested.

The records are shuffled and have opaque ids. Do not infer or reward the method, verbosity, apparent sophistication or family names proposed by a generator. Assign your own coarse semantic families jointly across ALL records in this task. Same core question with a new name, threshold, model, routine subgroup or time window remains the same family. A different intervention/comparison or scientific relation may be a different family if its central discriminating prediction changes. Same-family refinements can be useful: record them separately rather than dismissing them. Do not force everything with the same outcome into one family. Initial and final variants often belong together.

Judge candidate quality by four criteria: specific question/action, falsifiable contrast, coherent measurement/logic, feasible research plan with explicit necessary measurements. Current data need not settle the question, but a vague wish to collect unspecified new data is insufficient. Generic feature selection, fit-a-better-model or merely repeating a limitation in the dataset documentation is insufficient input increment. Existing conventional methods can form testable proposals, but do not count as established literature originality.

For final records, additionally inspect the actual tool request/code/output and final evidence claim. A code exit 0 is not scientific validation. Check if code computes the stated contrast, correct unit/independent sample, direction, temporal availability, target leakage, sample selection and causal scope. A computed feasibility count does not support an effect. A revised but uncomputed question may remain a useful proposal; it cannot inherit empirical support for a different question. Negative findings and correct withdrawals are useful evidence updates. Do not count withdrawn/blocked/null final candidates as delivered usable final ideas.

Main judgement usable_final requires a valid concrete final candidate AND no material mismatch between its claimed evidence status and actual evidence. A proposal-only final can pass when the plan is feasible and correctly labeled. A scientifically invalid evidence claim can fail even if the question itself is interesting. Report both proposal_quality and usable_final.

This review does not establish literature novelty or real-world causal effects. Do not penalize honest uncertainty. Do not invent statistical or code errors. If an issue cannot be settled from supplied records, label needs_check and state the exact unresolved issue.

Return JSON with:
- families: [{family_id, label, core_definition, boundary_rationale}]
- records: exactly one entry per opaque input id, each {id,family_id,criteria:{specific:boolean,falsifiable:boolean,coherent:boolean,feasible:boolean,input_increment:boolean},proposal_quality:boolean,usable_final:boolean|null,material_acceptance_error:boolean,error_type:string,reason:string,needs_check:string}.
- cross_record_observations: concise facts about repeated families and meaningful refinements without guessing strategies.

Every candidate id must occur exactly once; every family_id must exist. For a null final use family_id NONE, proposal_quality false, usable_final false, and define NONE. Explanations may be in Chinese. Limit each record's reason to around 45 English words or comparable Chinese length.

official_documentation.name: Wine Quality
official_documentation.abstract: Two datasets are included, related to red and white vinho verde wine samples, from the north of Portugal. The goal is to model wine quality based on physicochemical tests (see [Cortez et al., 2009], http://www3.dsi.uminho.pt/pcortez/wine/).

intro_paper.title: Modeling wine preferences by data mining from physicochemical properties
intro_paper.authors: P. Cortez, A. Cerdeira, Fernando Almeida, Telmo Matos, J. Reis

additional_info.summary:
The two datasets are related to red and white variants of the Portuguese "Vinho Verde" wine. For more details, consult: http://www.vinhoverde.pt/en/ or the reference [Cortez et al., 2009].  Due to privacy and logistic issues, only physicochemical (inputs) and sensory (the output) variables are available (e.g. there is no data about grape types, wine brand, wine selling price, etc.).

These datasets can be viewed as classification or regression tasks.  The classes are ordered and not balanced (e.g. there are many more normal wines than excellent or poor ones). Outlier detection algorithms could be used to detect the few excellent or poor wines. Also, we are not sure if all input variables are relevant. So it could be interesting to test feature selection methods.
additional_info.variable_info:
For more information, read [Cortez et al., 2009].
Input variables (based on physicochemical tests):
   1 - fixed acidity
   2 - volatile acidity
   3 - citric acid
   4 - residual sugar
   5 - chlorides
   6 - free sulfur dioxide
   7 - total sulfur dioxide
   8 - density
   9 - pH
   10 - sulphates
   11 - alcohol
Output variable (based on sensory data): 
   12 - quality (score between 0 and 10)

import json
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.optimize import minimize
from scipy.stats import chi2

df=TABLES['main'].copy()
chem=['fixed_acidity','volatile_acidity','citric_acid','residual_sugar','chlorides','free_sulfur_dioxide','total_sulfur_dioxide','density','pH','sulphates','alcohol']
df=df[chem+['quality','color']].dropna().copy()
keep=np.ones(len(df),dtype=bool)
for c in df.color.unique():
    ix=df.color.eq(c)
    for v in ['alcohol','residual_sugar']:
        lo,hi=df.loc[ix,v].quantile([.05,.95])
        keep &= ~(ix & ((df[v]<lo)|(df[v]>hi))).to_numpy()
df=df.loc[keep].reset_index(drop=True)
levels=sorted(int(v) for v in df.quality.unique())
y=np.searchsorted(levels,df.quality.to_numpy())
w=df.color.eq('white').to_numpy(float)
cols=[]; names=[]
for v in chem:
    z=df[v].to_numpy(float); sd=z.std()
    cols.append((z-z.mean())/(sd if sd else 1.)); names.append(v)
cols.append(w); names.append('white')
a=cols[names.index('alcohol')]; s=cols[names.index('residual_sugar')]
cols += [a*a,s*s]; names += ['alcohol_sq','sugar_sq']
terms=[a*s,a*s*s,a*a*s]
X0=np.column_stack(cols)
X1=np.column_stack(cols+terms+[w*t for t in terms])
def fit(X):
    n,p=X.shape; k=len(levels)-1
    cum=np.array([(y<=j).mean() for j in range(k)])
    cuts=np.log(np.clip(cum,1e-5,1-1e-5)/(1-np.clip(cum,1e-5,1-1e-5)))
    start=np.r_[np.zeros(p),cuts[0],np.log(np.maximum(np.diff(cuts),1e-3))]
    def unpack(t): return t[:p],np.r_[t[p],t[p]+np.cumsum(np.exp(np.clip(t[p+1:],-20,20)))]
    def loss(t):
        b,c=unpack(t); q=1/(1+np.exp(-np.clip(c[None,:]-X@b[:,None],-35,35)))
        pr=np.column_stack([q[:,0],np.diff(q,axis=1),1-q[:,-1]])
        return -np.log(np.maximum(pr[np.arange(n),y],1e-15)).sum()
    r=minimize(loss,start,method='L-BFGS-B',options={'maxiter':700,'ftol':1e-9})
    return {'success':bool(r.success),'message':str(r.message),'nll':float(r.fun),'beta':[float(v) for v in r.x[:p]]}
r0=fit(X0); r1=fit(X1); lr=max(0.,2*(r0['nll']-r1['nll']))
print(json.dumps({'n':int(len(df)),'counts_by_color':{str(k):int(v) for k,v in df.color.value_counts().items()},'quality_levels':levels,'range_rule':'within-color marginal 5th-95th percentiles for alcohol and residual_sugar','base_fit':r0,'expanded_fit':r1,'interaction_terms':['a*s','a*s^2','a^2*s','white*a*s','white*a*s^2','white*a^2*s'],'lr_stat_6df':float(lr),'lr_p_approx':float(chi2.sf(lr,6)),'warning':'Marginal ranges do not guarantee joint support; row independence and causal interpretation are unverified.'},separators=(',',':')))

import json
import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import minimize
from scipy.special import expit

chem=['fixed_acidity','volatile_acidity','citric_acid','residual_sugar','chlorides','free_sulfur_dioxide','total_sulfur_dioxide','density','pH','sulphates','alcohol']
results=[]
def fit_ord(X,y,k):
    n,p=X.shape
    counts=np.bincount(y,minlength=k).astype(float)
    cum=np.cumsum(counts)[:-1]/len(y)
    init_thr=np.log(np.clip(cum,1e-5,1-1e-5)/(1-np.clip(cum,1e-5,1-1e-5)))
    init=np.r_[np.zeros(p),init_thr[0],np.log(np.maximum(np.diff(init_thr),0.05))]
    def unpack(q):
        z=q[p:]
        th=np.r_[z[0],z[0]+np.cumsum(np.exp(np.clip(z[1:],-8,8)))]
        return q[:p],th
    def loss(q):
        b,th=unpack(q); c=expit(th[None,:]-X@b[:,None])
        probs=np.column_stack([c[:,0],np.diff(c,axis=1),1-c[:,-1]])
        return -np.log(np.clip(probs[np.arange(n),y],1e-12,1)).sum()
    r=minimize(loss,init,method='L-BFGS-B',options={'maxiter':250,'ftol':1e-8})
    return r.x[3],bool(r.success)
for color,g0 in DF.groupby('color'):
    g=g0.reset_index(drop=True); raw=g[chem].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mu=raw.mean(axis=0); sd=raw.std(axis=0); sd[sd==0]=1
    z=(raw-mu)/sd; ia=chem.index('volatile_acidity'); ic=chem.index('citric_acid')
    interaction=z[:,ia]*z[:,ic]
    cols=[z[:,ia],z[:,ic],interaction]+[z[:,j] for j in range(len(chem)) if j not in (ia,ic)]
    X=np.column_stack(cols); cats=sorted(g['quality'].astype(int).unique()); mp={v:i for i,v in enumerate(cats)}
    y=g['quality'].astype(int).map(mp).to_numpy(); k=len(cats)
    est,ok=fit_ord(X,y,k); rng=np.random.default_rng(20261102); boot=[]

import json
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors

rng = np.random.default_rng(20261102)
cols = ['fixed_acidity','volatile_acidity','citric_acid','residual_sugar','chlorides','free_sulfur_dioxide','total_sulfur_dioxide','density','pH','sulphates','alcohol']
out = {}
for color, g in TABLES['main'].groupby('color'):
    X = StandardScaler().fit_transform(g[cols].to_numpy(dtype=float))
    y = g['quality'].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    n = len(g)
    nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=2).fit(X).kneighbors(X, return_distance=False)[:, 1]
    pairs = sorted(set((min(i, int(j)), max(i, int(j))) for i, j in enumerate(nn)))
    a = np.array([p[0] for p in pairs], dtype=int)
    b = np.array([p[1] for p in pairs], dtype=int)
    observed = float(np.mean(np.abs(y[a] - y[b])))
    pcs = PCA(n_components=2).fit_transform(X)
    strata = np.zeros(n, dtype=int)
    for j in range(2):
        strata = strata * 4 + pd.qcut(pcs[:, j], q=4, labels=False, duplicates='drop').astype(int)
    groups = [np.flatnonzero(strata == s) for s in np.unique(strata)]
    perm = []
    for _ in range(500):
        yp = y.copy()
        for ix in groups:
            yp[ix] = rng.permutation(yp[ix])
        perm.append(float(np.mean(np.abs(yp[a] - yp[b]))))
    perm = np.asarray(perm)
    out[str(color)] = {'n_rows': n, 'n_unique_pairs': len(pairs), 'n_strata': len(groups), 'min_stratum_n': int(min(map(len, groups))), 'observed_mean_abs_quality_difference': observed, 'permutation_mean': float(perm.mean()), 'permutation_interval_95': [float(np.quantile(perm, .025)), float(np.quantile(perm, .975))], 'fraction_permutations_at_least_as_favorable': float(np.mean(perm <= observed))}
print(json.dumps(out, separators=(',', ':')))

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.optimize import minimize

df=TABLES['main'].copy()
chem=['fixed_acidity','volatile_acidity','citric_acid','residual_sugar','chlorides','free_sulfur_dioxide','total_sulfur_dioxide','density','pH','sulphates','alcohol']
df=df[chem+['quality','color']].dropna().copy()
levels=sorted(int(v) for v in df.quality.unique())
cols=[]; names=[]
for v in chem:
    z=df[v].to_numpy(float); sd=z.std()
    cols.append((z-z.mean())/(sd if sd else 1.)); names.append(v)
cols.append(df.color.eq('white').to_numpy(float)); names.append('white')
X=np.column_stack([np.ones(len(df))]+cols)
va_idx=names.index('volatile_acidity')+1
results=[]
for j in levels[:-1]:
    y=(df.quality.to_numpy()>j).astype(float)
    n1=int(y.sum()); n0=int(len(y)-n1)
    def loss(b):
        z=np.clip(X@b,-35,35)
        return float(np.logaddexp(0,z).sum()-y@z)
    def grad(b):
        z=np.clip(X@b,-35,35)
        p=1/(1+np.exp(-z))
        return X.T@(p-y)
    r=minimize(loss,np.zeros(X.shape[1]),jac=grad,method='BFGS',options={'maxiter':500,'gtol':1e-7})
    try:
        H=X.T@((lambda p:p*(1-p))(1/(1+np.exp(-np.clip(X@r.x,-35,35))))[:,None]*X)
        cov=np.linalg.pinv(H)
        se=float(np.sqrt(max(cov[va_idx,va_idx],0)))
    except Exception:
        se=None
    results.append({'threshold':int(j),'n_quality_le_threshold':n0,'n_quality_gt_threshold':n1,'converged':bool(r.success),'message':str(r.message),'volatile_acidity_beta':float(r.x[va_idx]),'model_based_se':se})
print(json.dumps({'n':int(len(df)),'quality_levels':levels,'same_rows_all_thresholds':True,'predictors':chem+['white'],'threshold_results':results,'warning':'Descriptive separate cumulative logits; thresholds share rows, model-based standard errors assume independent rows, and neither causality nor lot-level inference is established.'},separators=(',',':')))
